headline: UK and Google DeepMind report early PlanAssist results as live pilot expands to 15 councils
summary: The UK government says early PlanAssist testing in Barnet, Camden and Dorset cut officer time on key householder-application tasks by 58% and links that result to a reduction in routine processing from eight weeks to four. Google DeepMind reports that more than 70% of generated reports needed no edits. Both are involved-party claims without disclosed pilot denominators or comparison design. The official tender defines the eight-to-four-week target around stages the tool can affect and excludes consultation, site visits, neighbour notification, external-consultee responses and committee scheduling, so the broader end-to-end implication is not established. PlanningLens reports a 7.71-week pre-trial median across 7,663 decisions and a matched 16-council panel frozen before outcomes; its early May–July data are not attributed to the tool, and it says results are too early. The official award notice lists £8.288 million including VAT for a contract to Google Cloud EMEA Limited, not realized spend or proven value. The live test expands to 15 councils for 12 months, with officers retaining review and decision authority.
